valores.label: Los Angeles total area after both consolidations (1909-08-28)

fonte: Los Angeles Daily Times; Los Angeles County Public Works (annexation records)
legenda: Wilmington 107–61; Los Angeles 13,661–221; San Pedro 726–227. Aug. 28, 1909: 76 sq mi and a coastline.
credito_tela: Source: Los Angeles Times, Aug. 5 and 13, 1909 · Source: Los Angeles County annexation records
nota: O 13.661 × 221 de Los Angeles foi o voto sobre Wilmington (98,4 %); a voz diz 'Los Angeles said yes the same day, by a landslide', sem dizer que cobriu as duas fusões. Para San Pedro, o Times de 13/08 dá a 'tremendous majority' de Los Angeles; o número de Los Angeles nesse dia não vai à tela.
narracao: That August, each of the three cities voted, and each had to say yes on its own. Wilmington voted on August 4: 107 to 61. Los Angeles said yes the same day, by a landslide. San Pedro, on August 12: 726 to 227. On August 28, 1909, both consolidations took effect, and Los Angeles, now seventy-six square miles, had a coastline of its own for the first time.
